resources.string: Your direct chat over Wi-Fi Direct is ready with %1$s.

1. Keep both Android devices nearby with Wi-Fi on.
2. Create a link on one device and search for it from the other.
3. Accept the Android connection request.
4. If the device does not support Wi-Fi Direct, try Same Wi-Fi.

1. Open Qetara on both devices.
2. Check that they share the same network. Guest networks may prevent them from finding each other.
3. On a PC, allow Qetara to access the local network.
4. If the device does not appear, enter the IP address shown on the other device.
Enter the receiving device’s code and PIN.
Ready to send files and messages.
Between nearby Android devices, without a router.
Android and PC on the same Wi-Fi network.
Tap Activate session to connect. In the meantime, you can prepare files and view messages and Downloads.
Android needs your permission to find nearby devices and create a Wi-Fi Direct link.
You can also choose Same Wi-Fi to share with a PC.
Open Android settings, turn on Wi-Fi, and return to Qetara. No internet connection is needed.
Preparing the session. If the other device is Android, accept the connection request there.
Below, enter the session code and PIN shown by Qetara on the receiving device.
The session is not confirmed yet. Accept the request on the other Android device or enter the receiver’s credentials here.
Session confirmed. You can now share.
Choose the device that will receive your files and messages. Your previous selection stays the same until you change it.
On the other Android device, open Qetara, choose Wi-Fi Direct, and tap Find a device. Then choose this device.
Accept the Android request if it appears. Keep Qetara open on both devices.
The link already exists. Approve the connection on the device that opened the link to start sharing.
On the other Android device, tap Create a link. Devices will appear here.
Choose the device that created the link below.
Create a link on one device and search for it from the other.
Open Qetara on the other device too. It can be an Android device or a PC; the network does not need internet access.
Open Qetara on the other device. On a PC, turn on Receive.
The session ended. Renew it to keep sharing.
For a PC, enter its session code and PIN. Between Android devices, you can accept the connection request to share the session.
Copy the credentials Qetara shows on the receiver. The code and PIN must match on both devices.
Check that Qetara is open on the same Wi-Fi. You can also connect by IP address.
Enter an IPv4 address, for example 192.168.1.8.
It appears in Qetara on the other device.
Before remembering this device, check that you started the transfer from it.
Creating a link on this device.
Searching for devices using Wi-Fi Direct.
Permission is needed to use Wi-Fi Direct.
Open system Wi-Fi settings to use Wi-Fi Direct.
Wi-Fi Direct is ready to create or find a link.
Searching for devices on this Wi-Fi network.
Connect both devices to the same Wi-Fi network.
A direct link is also available.
Wi-Fi Direct is still available as an alternative.
Wi-Fi is available as an alternative.
You can also use the same Wi-Fi network.
You need nearby network permission to use Wi-Fi Direct.
Android manages Wi-Fi Direct through the system. Open Wi-Fi first, then return here.
On the other device, tap Find link, then Connect.
Wait while both devices finish linking.
Keep the link open on the other device. When it appears, tap Connect.
If this device starts the connection, tap Create link. If the other device already started, tap Find link.
On the other device, tap Find link to finish connecting.
Connect both devices to the same Wi-Fi network to find devices by IP.
Connect to a device on this Wi-Fi
Search for devices or use a suggested IP.
Renew the session to keep using chat and transfers.
Review failed items and retry them from the queue view.
You selected files, but there is no valid destination IP yet.
You can now start sending to the connected device.
Nearby network permission is required to find and connect devices using Wi-Fi Direct.
Connect both devices to the same Wi-Fi network to use IP addresses and LAN discovery.
First open system Wi-Fi settings. Then create or find a link.
Search for devices on this Wi-Fi network. The Wi-Fi channel uses this network.
You can now try chat, sending, or history without leaving this screen.
Renew the session to continue using chat and transfers.
Sending files in the background. You can check the queue.
This device has created the link. On the other device, tap Find link.
Wait while this device joins the link.
Choose the device that created the link and tap Connect.
Find the other device to join its link.
Android manages Wi-Fi Direct through the system. Open Wi-Fi and return here.
This device has created the link. The other device still needs to join.
Search for devices on this Wi-Fi network or use a known IP address.
Use the active tab or the main action in the header.
First open system Wi-Fi settings. When Wi-Fi Direct is available, you can create or find a link.
When Direct is connected, Qetara uses it first for messages and files.
This device has created the link, but the other device still needs to finish joining.
Choose the device that created the link and tap Connect to finish joining.
Find the other device to join its direct link.
Use Create link if this device starts the connection. Use Find link if the other device already started.
While you are viewing Wi-Fi, Direct is already ready and will be used first for sending and chatting.
Use the same Wi-Fi network to find devices by IP and share with PCs or other devices.
Use Wi-Fi when both devices share the same local network.
Current channel: outside the Wi-Fi channel
Session expired: renew the session to reactivate chat.
Connect this device to a Wi-Fi network to use the channel.
Join the Wi-Fi channel to participate.
You can write even if you are still alone.
Send text to devices that have already joined the Wi-Fi channel.
Your direct chat over Wi-Fi Direct is ready.
Your direct link has been created. The other device still needs to join to open direct chat.
The current mode is Wi-Fi Direct. The channel is ready for chat.
The current mode is Wi-Fi Direct. Connect the other device first to enable chat.
The current mode is Wi-Fi. Connect both devices to the same network.
The network is ready, but a device is needed for one-to-one chat.
The direct channel over Wi-Fi LAN is ready.
